---
id: "smk-12"
title: "The Volga"
---

The Volga is the longest river in Europe, flowing for about 3,530 kilometres entirely within Russia. It rises in the Valdai Hills north-west of Moscow and winds south-east across the Russian plain to the Caspian Sea, into which it discharges through a large delta near Astrakhan. Along its course lie several of Russia's largest cities, including Nizhny Novgorod, Kazan, Samara and Volgograd. A chain of reservoirs built in the twentieth century turned much of the river into a series of lakes that provide hydroelectric power and allow navigation for most of the year, although ice closes the waterway in winter. The Volga basin drains roughly a third of European Russia and supports agriculture, fishing and heavy industry. Canals connect the river to the Baltic Sea, the White Sea, the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea, so the Volga is central to the inland shipping network of the country.
